# Legacy factory compatibility (Go migration)

Scenario v2 does not use factories. Author new integrations with ordinary code inside `autonoma.DefineScenario` as described in `implement.md` and `scenarios.md`.

This page exists only for projects migrating older customer code that already calls `autonoma.DefineFactory`. The helper is not registered with the handler, is not discoverable, and is never invoked by the v2 protocol. Do not introduce it in a new v2 integration.

## Temporary use during migration

Existing helper calls may remain temporarily while their creation and cleanup behavior moves into scenario-owned functions. New v2 code should call those functions directly from `Up` and `Down`.

## The shape

`DefineFactory` takes four arguments and returns an `autonoma.FactoryDefinition`:

```go
type UserInput struct {
    Email string
    OrgID string
}

userFactory := autonoma.DefineFactory(
    func(input interface{}, ctx autonoma.FactoryContext) (map[string]any, error) {
        in := input.(*UserInput)
        user, err := createUser(in.Email, in.OrgID) // your real creation code
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        return map[string]any{"id": user.ID, "email": user.Email}, nil
    },
    reflect.TypeOf(UserInput{}), // InputStruct - required
    func(record interface{}, ctx autonoma.FactoryContext) error {
        rec := record.(map[string]any)
        id, _ := rec["id"].(string)
        return deleteUser(id)
    },
    nil, // RefStruct - optional
)
```

- The first argument (`Create`) runs your real creation code and must return a `map[string]any` with at least an `"id"` key.
- The second argument (`InputStruct`, a `reflect.Type`) is required. `Create` receives a pointer to a freshly unmarshaled instance of it, so a type assertion (`input.(*UserInput)`) recovers your typed input.
- The third argument (`Teardown`) optionally deletes the record. Pass `nil` and the factory creates but does not delete.
- The fourth argument (`RefStruct`, a `reflect.Type`) is optional; when set, the stored record is unmarshaled through it before `Teardown` is called, so `Teardown` receives a `*RefStruct` instead of the raw map.

`DefineFactory` panics if `Create` is nil or `InputStruct` is not a struct type (or pointer to one). `ctx` is an `autonoma.FactoryContext`: `{ Refs map[string][]map[string]any; ScenarioName string; TestRunID string }`. A factory that needs a database connection gets it from your host app (its own GORM, sqlx, pgx, ...); the SDK does not ship one.

## Using a factory from a scenario

A factory is a plain value you call yourself; wire its output into your scenario's `Teardown` so `Down` can undo it.

```go
var WithUser = autonoma.DefineScenario(autonoma.ScenarioDefinition{
    Name:        "with-user",
    Description: "One user created through the user factory",
    Up: func(ctx autonoma.ScenarioUpContext) (autonoma.ScenarioUpResult, error) {
        fctx := autonoma.FactoryContext{Refs: map[string][]map[string]any{}, ScenarioName: "with-user", TestRunID: ctx.TestRunID}
        record, err := userFactory.Create(&UserInput{
            Email: autonoma.UniqueEmail(ctx.TestRunID, "", ""),
            OrgID: "org_1",
        }, fctx)
        if err != nil {
            return autonoma.ScenarioUpResult{}, err
        }
        return autonoma.ScenarioUpResult{
            Teardown: map[string]any{"user": record},
        }, nil
    },
    Down: func(ctx autonoma.ScenarioDownContext) error {
        record, _ := ctx.Teardown["user"].(map[string]any)
        if userFactory.Teardown == nil {
            return nil
        }
        return userFactory.Teardown(record, autonoma.FactoryContext{ScenarioName: ctx.Name, TestRunID: ctx.TestRunID})
    },
})
```

`autonoma.FactoryRegistry` (a `map[string]FactoryDefinition`) exists as a convenience for grouping factories by model name, but nothing in the protocol reads it - it is yours to iterate however your `Up`/`Down` need. For most scenarios a direct call in `Up` and a matching delete in `Down` is clearer than reaching for a factory at all.
